tasks.short: Teach socially acceptable behavior through responsive reinforcement

steps.what: Assess the immediate situation and choose appropriate behavior reinforcement
Teach socially acceptable behavior through modeling and positive reinforcement
Observe the pupil's response and adjust the immediate teaching approach

tasks.design: Retain immediate assessment, reinforcement and response monitoring with the teacher. A template in {DOCS} cannot replace responsive instruction; this task does not require a separate reinforcement log after every interaction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The essential work is situational teaching rather than repeated data handling.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated software change removes the direct teaching work.
tasks.still_hard: A child's understanding, distress and response change during the interaction.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize the child and adapt reinforcement sensitively.

reach.learn: Notice when the planned response is inappropriate

evidence.claim: Responsive reinforcement remains human work; no task-specific saving is established.

assumptions: The boundary is the teaching interaction and immediate response. A formal incident report, when required, is distinct work, not a log invented for every interaction.
The teacher produces the situation assessment in s1 and observes the response in s3, with all observation time retained. No machine depends on an uncaptured behavior classification.
No current lookup, written artifact or till setting is identified in this immediate teaching task. A document template or native record view therefore removes no priced operation.
No software or new capture is introduced, so recurring upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Whether the school requires a separate record for specified incidents
research_questions: Does direct observation identify any actual repeated lookup within this teaching task?

already_counted.description: Assess and monitor the child's response

incremental.description: No new system or capture requirement

approvals.approved_version: Exact instruction and reinforcement delivered to the current pupil; teacher reconsiders changed content or circumstances during delivery

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=100 and no upkeep gives zero net. Both familiar routines and unexpected pupil responses retain assessment, direct teaching and observation; no existing record operation has been identified to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish classroom behavior rules and enforce them responsively

steps.what: Establish appropriate rules and procedures for the current students
Write the classroom rules and visual routine instructions used with students
Explain and enforce behavior rules and procedures among students

tasks.design: Reuse the existing visual routine layout in {DOCS} when writing the classroom rules. The teacher chooses the rules, writes their actual content and retains explanation and enforcement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recreating familiar display layout repeats a small formatting operation.
tasks.enabler_now: An existing editable classroom layout can preserve headings and visual placement.
tasks.still_hard: Rules must fit individual communication and support needs.
tasks.human_edge: Apply rules fairly and recognize when a pupil needs a different response.
tasks.altitude: Reduce display formatting without delegating discipline.

reach.learn: Distinguish the routine from an individual adaptation

evidence.claim: Reusing an existing document layout can remove repeated formatting but not rule selection or enforcement.

assumptions: The displayed rules are an existing classroom teaching artifact read by students and staff, not a new discipline log.

The teacher reads policy and pupil needs in s1, produces rule text in s2 and observes current behavior in s3; all capture and interpretation are counted. Missing or unsuitable visual assets are handled manually.
Reusing visual positions and headings removes 2 of 20 display-writing hours; writing, accessibility checking and ordinary same-system saves retain 18. No self-approval is imposed on that save.
The layout is maintained during normal classroom preparation; no separate recurring configuration work is introduced.
unknowns: Whether a compatible editable visual layout already exists
research_questions: Does layout reuse remove two hours per hundred baseline hours after accessibility adjustments?

already_counted.description: Write and check usable classroom rules

incremental.description: Existing document layout needs no additional recurring service

approvals.approved_version: Exact rules explanation and enforcement delivered to current students; changed content or pupil circumstances require teacher reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=98, no additional upkeep gives 2 net. Incompatible visual formats or individual symbol changes retain all 20 writing hours and yield zero; a partially reusable layout retaining 18.5 writing hours plus the other 80 yields 1.5 net. Rule selection and direct enforcement remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate pupil performance and development

steps.what: Review existing student goals and prior performance observations
Observe students' performance, behavior, social development and physical health
Evaluate observed performance and development against individual goals
Write observations and the teacher evaluation in existing pupil records

tasks.design: Use a native goal-and-observation view and existing pupil-note fields in {LMS}. The teacher observes, evaluates and writes the substantive findings; reusable identity and goal context remove repeated handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding prior goals and re-entering stable note context repeats work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pupil records support goal tracking and structured observation entries.
tasks.still_hard: An observation is contextual and cannot establish a diagnosis or inferred emotion.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret change in a child's own circumstances.
tasks.altitude: Make observation records easier to use while retaining evaluation.

reach.learn: Trace conclusions to actual dated observations

evidence.claim: ParnasSys offers pupil records and learning-goal tracking; the proposed local savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: The existing observation record informs the teacher's next teaching and support review. No additional daily reporting log is created.

The teacher verifies pupil identity, goal identifier and observation date in s1 and captures observed facts and evaluation in s4. Capture is included in 15 retained writing hours; absent goal metadata is entered or found manually.
The native view removes 1.5 of 10 lookup hours. Reusable identity, goal headings and date context remove 5 of 20 record-writing hours; all observation narrative and evaluation remain human.
Ordinary same-system saves remain included without an approval stage. No automatic scoring, alert, message or emotion classification is named.
unknowns: Compatibility of current goal fields and observation forms
research_questions: Do the native fields reduce total lookup and writing while preserving accurate dated evidence?

already_counted.description: Capture and verify actual observations and teacher evaluation

incremental.description: Maintain the goal view and observation headings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=93.5, gross 6.5 less 1 upkeep gives 5.5 net. Conservative case: inconsistent goal metadata retains all lookup time and 19 writing hours, with upkeep consuming the one hour removed. With compatible goal links retaining 9 lookup hours and 16.5 writing hours, other 70 plus 1 upkeep yield 3.5 net. Direct observation and evaluation remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with families and professionals to develop individual educational plans

steps.what: Review students' current goals, assessments and support needs for educational planning
Confer with parents and professionals to determine individual educational needs and goals
Write the individual educational plan from discussed goals and support decisions
Check the final plan's goals, support details and intended recipients before sharing
Share the checked educational plan with its intended family and professional recipients

tasks.design: Use the existing plan module and linked pupil context in {LMS} to reduce navigation and repeated plan fields. The teacher retains consultation, substantive plan writing and final version checking, then separately shares the checked plan through {EMAIL} or the current pupil system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning evidence and stable plan fields are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pupil and plan modules can reuse established fields without generating support decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Families and professionals may disagree about suitable goals and support.
tasks.human_edge: Develop a workable individual plan with the people involved.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated plan handling while protecting consultation.

reach.learn: Keep source evidence, disagreements and final plan version explicit

evidence.claim: ParnasSys describes pupil records and an OPP module; this supports native plan handling, not automated support judgement.

assumptions: The plan is the artifact explicitly required by this task and read by the family and support team. No separate meeting minutes or activity log is added.

The teacher verifies identity, current goals and assessment dates in s1, obtains proposed goals and support decisions in s2 and captures them in s3. All capture stays within 22.5 retained writing hours; absent source fields are manually reconciled.

Linked context removes 3 of 15 preparation hours; reusable pupil identity, existing plan structure and unchanged context remove 7.5 of 30 writing hours. Goals, support choices, disagreements and factual checking remain human.

Final sharing is separate and fully retained. Ordinary author saves in the plan module remain included in writing without self-approval; s4 checks the version for external sharing, not permission to save.
unknowns: Actual time spent on stable fields versus new support content
research_questions: Does native reuse reduce total plan preparation after source reconciliation and family-specific rewriting?

already_counted.description: Write substantive plan content and check the version to share

incremental.description: Maintain linked context and plan field layout

approvals.approved_version: Exact pupil information and proposals disclosed to verified current meeting participants; changed participants or content require reconsideration
Exact final plan version and verified recipient set checked in s4; edits or recipient changes invalidate the check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=89.5, gross 10.5 less 2 upkeep gives 8.5 net. When legacy plans lack compatible fields, preparation retains 15 and writing 28 hours; other 55 and 2 upkeep yield zero. Compatible plan structure retaining 13 preparation and 24 writing hours plus other 55 and 2 upkeep yields 6 net. Consultation, final checking and actual sharing stay fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep direct special education and individualized judgement with the teacher while reducing actual pupil-record repetition.
reach: Connect observations to usable support plans
skills_to_grow: Distinguish observed facts from inferred diagnoses
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with clear pupil evidence and usable individual plans who remains responsible for responsive classroom teaching.
